contraindications.note: Non-selective beta-blocker causes potent bronchoconstriction; contraindicated in asthma and COPD.
Beta-blocker carries risk of bronchospasm in reactive airway disease.
Beta-blocker contraindicated in asthma and reactive airway disease.
Beta-blocker carries risk of bronchoconstriction in reactive airway disease.
NSAID causes gastric mucosal ulceration, erosions, and GI hemorrhage.
NSAID inhibits protective prostaglandins, aggravating peptic ulcer and GI bleeding.
Direct mucosal injury and antiplatelet effect increase severe GI hemorrhage risk.
Non-selective NSAID increases gastrointestinal ulceration and bleeding risk.
NSAID contraindicated in active gastrointestinal ulcer or bleeding.
Risk of fatal lactic acidosis in renal failure; contraindicated in severe renal disease.
NSAID reduces renal blood flow and precipitates acute renal decompensation.
Sympathomimetic agent may elevate blood pressure and exacerbate hypertension.
Corticosteroids increase risk of peptic ulceration and GI bleeding, especially with NSAIDs.

demographic_rules.note: Contraindicated in children with fever or viral infections due to risk of Reye's syndrome.
Fluoroquinolone carries risk of arthropathy and cartilage damage in pediatric patients.
Beers Criteria: Increased sensitivity to benzodiazepines in elderly; high risk of falls, delirium, and cognitive impairment.
Beers Criteria: Long-acting benzodiazepine causes prolonged sedation and marked fall risk in older adults.
Beers Criteria: High risk of delirium, central nervous system depression, and reduced seizure threshold in elderly.
Beers Criteria: Chronic NSAID use in elderly increases risk of GI bleeding and accelerated renal function decline.
